description: Public dashboard tracking groundwater depletion in Romania and Hungary from NASA GRACE-FO data assimilation, at NUTS-2 resolution.
current_focus: Get a native read of the RO/HU copy - now four strings larger after the design pass (skipToContent, nav.sections, pinHint, pinnedHint). Still the last launch blocker and the only thing between this and a press pitch. As of 2026-08-01 the design pass IS finally live and verified there (it had been committed but never pushed for about an hour, which made the live site look like it had no tooltips - it had no client script at all); the band legend no longer orphans its last swatch at any width or locale; the homepage shows NASA's Europe map; both data workflows are green. Three lower-priority items are queued behind the native read: astro check has never run (the script exists but @astrojs/check and typescript are not installed, and astro build only strips types - bump as its own change since it touches package-lock), the GitHub Actions Node 20 deprecation (now firing as an annotation on EVERY deploy for checkout@v4, configure-pages@v5, setup-node@v4 and upload-artifact@v4, all forced onto Node 24 - still its own change because the Pages actions move together and a bad bump breaks publishing), and confirming the deploy ref fix under a real workflow_call, which can only happen when the bot itself commits on a Monday archive run.

features.name: data-pipeline
features.description: GES DISC ingest, NUTS-2 zonal stats, UNL operational mirror, timeseries compile.
features.notes: All commands run as documented with PYTHONPATH unset. Archive covers 2003-02-03 to 2026-05-25, 1217 weeks x 16 regions. A full no-op run leaves data byte-identical.

features.name: backfill-ci-safety
features.description: Resume from timeseries.json and merge on compile, so a checkout without the gitignored weekly files cannot destroy the archive.
features.notes: Tested against a simulated fresh checkout containing only committed files: resume resolves to 2026-05-25, and a no-op run preserves all 1217 weeks, 16 regions, no duplicates, identical values.

features.name: workflow-mirror
features.description: Daily UNL operational map refresh, 06:23 UTC, idempotent, no secrets needed.
features.notes: Ran green in CI in 23s: skipped correctly as already current, freshness passed, build passed, and it made no commit. FIXED 2026-08-01: was mirroring UNL's /data/Web/ tree, which is the CONTIGUOUS US product - the homepage showed a map of the United States under 'NASA's current map' in all three locales. Now pulls the EU cut of the global run, /globaldata/<stamp>/GRACE_GWS_EU_<stamp>.png. EU and CONUS verified publishing in lockstep across the 8 weeks to 2026-07-27; dist PNG sha matches the EU download. is_current() now also compares recorded URLs, because week+files-exist alone could not detect the source change and would have skipped forever.

features.name: workflow-archive
features.description: Weekly GES DISC archive catch-up, Mondays 06:43 UTC, regenerates the share card.
features.notes: Secrets set 2026-08-01. First real run (30705952636) went green in 42s: Earthdata auth, backfill resume, freshness, card regen, build and commit all passed. timeseries.json came through byte-identical at 1217 weeks x 16 regions, no duplicates, so resume-and-merge holds under a real CI checkout. Its only commit was the share-card PNG re-encoding (see share-card notes).

features.name: workflow-deploy
features.description: GitHub Pages build and deploy; called explicitly by both data workflows.
features.notes: Green across several runs; all 13 live URLs return 200. Called explicitly because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes do not trigger workflows. FIXED 2026-08-01: checkout is now pinned to ref: main. It defaulted to github.sha, which under workflow_call is the SHA that started the run - frozen before the bot's data commit - so the deploy published the previous week's tree. Proven by the refspec changing from a pinned SHA to +refs/heads/main*. A true workflow_call end-to-end test still needs a run where the bot actually commits. 2026-08-01 (fifth) LANDMINE, and it is not a workflow bug: deploys only fire on push, so an unpushed commit means the live site silently serves the previous build. The entire design pass sat committed and unpushed for about an hour and the live site had NO client script, no .map-region and no .readout - which presented as 'there are no tooltips'. Before debugging anything reported broken on the live site, run: git fetch -q origin && git log origin/main..main --oneline, plus gh run list. A local npm run build proves nothing about production. Related: a reused headless Chrome --user-data-dir caches across launches, so send Network.setCacheDisabled or delete the profile before verifying a live URL, or you will 'confirm' a deploy failed when it succeeded.

features.name: computed-lede
features.description: Homepage headline computed from the archive via guarded claim templates; superlatives only appear when true.
features.notes: All three templates exercised against real archive weeks (rank 1 -> superlative, rank 3 -> ordinal, current -> floor). As-of scoping confirmed to not look ahead.

features.name: baseline-correction
features.description: Baseline period settled at 1948-2014 for V3.0; '75-year' removed sitewide.
features.notes: Confirmed against three NASA sources. drought.gov's 1948-2012 describes a pre-V3.0, Princeton-forced release. Reasoning recorded in docs/methodology.md.

features.name: share-card
features.description: Generated 1200x630 OG card plus absolute social metadata, guarded so a stale card fails the build.
features.notes: Serves 200 as image/png at 1200x630, ratio 1.905, 107 KB. Build fails when the card for the newest week is missing. Regenerates deterministically PER PLATFORM but not across them: macOS rsvg 109516 bytes vs ubuntu runner 108712 for the same week, so the first CI run after a local regen makes one no-op churn commit. 2026-08-01: baseline note wrapped onto two lines - it ran to x=546, 14px past the panel edge at 532, onto the map background. Now x=302/307. All 17 values of 'N of 16' checked: widest 508px, 24px clear.

features.name: site-i18n
features.description: Plain-language copy in EN/RO/HU. English at root, /ro/ and /hu/ prefixed. Methodology is EN-only by choice.
features.notes: 10 routes build, zero broken internal links, correct hreflang with x-default, per-locale og:locale and canonicals. CAVEAT: translations are machine-authored and have NOT been reviewed by a native speaker. 2026-08-01 design pass added FOUR new strings to that queue - skipToContent, nav.sections, pinHint, pinnedHint. The hero deliberately reuses existing strings and needed none: its eyebrow is 'NASA GRACE-FO' plus a date, and the big number is a pull-quote of the existing claim sentence rather than a split of it, because splitting a translated sentence breaks on Hungarian word order.

features.name: timelapse-playback
features.description: Visitor-controlled playback of all 1217 weeks with 0.5x-4x speed; progressive enhancement over the static map.
features.notes: Payload, markup and timing verified: 16 columns match 16 rendered paths, no malformed rows, caption date-swap resolves to exactly one match in all three locales, and timing simulated at 60/120 Hz across all speeds lands within 0.1s. Click and drag confirmed working in a real browser by the user on 2026-08-01, closing the last gap. 2026-08-01 design pass: the transport was rebuilt - round play button, a large tabular year readout, and a scrub track that is itself a 23-year ribbon of the national average (consecutive same-band weeks collapsed into runs server-side). The fragile caption date-swap was KEPT rather than replaced, because it was already verified in all three locales; it now drives any [data-tl-datetext] element inside the map block. That fixed a real pre-existing bug: the country-page map heading said 'week of 25 May 2026' while the map showed 2009. The heading now lives inside RegionMap. The TABLE heading deliberately does not track, because the table does not scrub.

features.name: charts
features.description: Trailing 52-week trend line per country and a year x month heatmap, server-rendered SVG.
features.notes: Values cross-checked independently against timeseries.json (heatmap May 2026 = 5.4 both ways; trend endpoints 5.9/1.3). Rasterised and visually inspected for collisions and overflow. Palette validated against the site's own surface. The 12-column heatmap confirmed in a real browser by the user on 2026-08-01. On country pages the charts now sit BELOW the region table, matching the homepage order. 2026-08-01: trend end labels now carry a unit ('Románia 6/100') - the bare number could read as a rank or a score out of 10. Sizing at the same time fixed a latent clip: labels are 11px font-weight:600 over Georgia, which has no semibold, so it resolves to Georgia BOLD, at which 'Magyarország 1' was 87.8px against 82px available. viewBox widened 760->820 and PAD.right 92->146 so plot width is unchanged (634->640) and the worst case 'Magyarország 100/100' ends at 813.3 of 820. 2026-08-01 design pass: both charts now sit in panels and carry hover readouts. Three fixes worth keeping: end labels are decluttered around their midpoint because in a drought both countries sit near the floor and 'Romania 6/100' and 'Hungary 1/100' overprinted; the 'an ordinary year' annotation is drawn AFTER the series paths, since a paper halo can only mask what is already painted and the Hungary line was striking through it; and the legend now carries each series' current value, which is what a phone reader gets because the in-chart end labels are hidden under 40rem where the 820-unit viewBox would render them at about 5px (the chart scrolls in its own container there).

features.name: operational-ingest
features.description: Read UNL's operational percentile GeoTIFF and aggregate it to NUTS-2 through the same zonal.aggregate the archive uses.
features.notes: pipeline/operational.py + pipeline/verify_operational.py. Grid alignment proven: per-region valid_cells match the archive exactly. NOT wired into the site, deliberately - a current-week readout needs new EN/RO/HU copy and the RO/HU translations are still awaiting a native read. MUST NOT be spliced onto the archive series: measured over 768 region-weeks the two products differ by median 1.44 percentile points, p90 7.05, max 24.5, against the original plan's own <1 tolerance, and the disagreement is SEASONAL, which would poison the rolling mean and the year x month heatmap specifically. Present agreement looks good (median 0.14 at the join) only because RO/HU are saturated near percentile 0 in the current drought. Full write-up in docs/path-b-plan.md.

features.name: design-system
features.description: Warm-paper design system for the whole site: layout grid, type scale, hero band, readout cards, transport bar.
features.notes: Added 2026-08-01. public/styles.css is now tokens + a CSS-grid layout with content/wide/full tracks - the fix for everything living in a 78ch column, which rendered the map ~330px wide on a 1440px screen. Map is now ~720px in a full-bleed hero. Serif carries prose, sans carries every number and control, both from system stacks (no webfont). Every heading starts on one left edge (--wide); graphics cap at --graphic. Direction was the user's call: warm paper everywhere, no dark mode; the hero itself is the reel-capture frame rather than a separate cinema mode. Verified over CDP in a real browser across EN/RO/HU: zero console errors and zero horizontal overflow on 8 pages x 5 widths (390/768/1024/1440/1920), 101 internal links and assets with zero broken, and the no-JS path still renders 16 regions, 15 score labels, legends and 305 native title tooltips. 2026-08-01 (fifth): the band legend was rebuilt because six bands never fit one row under the hero map in ANY locale - 740px EN, 778 RO, 838 HU against the map column's 720 - so flex orphaned 'near normal' on its own second row, breaking right after 'abnormally dry'. Now three regimes: phone = one column with the threshold flush right (two columns are impossible, half a row is 156-171px against Hungarian's 195px label); 34-62rem = 2-3 aligned columns; 62rem up = one row except the hero map's own legend, since the country map (1024px) and chart panels (901-980px) clear 838px and the hero map does not. 336 legend instances verified on the LIVE site across 6 pages x 3 locales x 28 widths (280-1920). LANDMINE 1: the severity hex values live in FOUR places that must move together - bandColor() in lib/data.ts, the BANDS table in RegionMap.astro's client script, the severity tokens in public/styles.css, and pipeline/share_card.py. LANDMINE 2: the phone legend block MUST stay below the base .legend-item rules - media queries add no specificity, so the first version was silently overridden by source order and did nothing.

features.name: map-interaction
features.description: Styled readout card for map, trend line and heatmap, with pinning, keyboard access and table-row linking.
features.notes: Added 2026-08-01. Native <title> tooltips are removed on JS init and replaced by one card (name, score, band pill, weeks-in-a-row); click to pin, Esc to release, focusable paths, and hovering a table row drives the map. Emphasis is by dimming the rest - a region's fill is its value and must never change on hover. Map labels are fitted at build time against each region's path bbox via the new pathBBox() in lib/data.ts, so a label that does not fit is not drawn: HU11 Budapest is the only region on the combined map too small for a score, RO32 the only one on the Romania map too small for a name. Every card value was recomputed independently from timeseries.json (Budapest 0.4 / 48-week streak, Nyugat-Dunantul 0.9 / 70, May 2012 trend RO 24.2 and HU 16.5, 2022-March heatmap 7.8). Focus-ring removal is scoped to .map-svg[data-enhanced] so no-JS keyboard users keep an indicator.
